pillars.title: Cheaper to run
pillars.text: Electricity per kilometre costs a fraction of petrol or diesel, and most owners charge overnight at home. Fewer moving parts also means simpler servicing.

pillars.title: Two-wheelers lead the way
pillars.text: India's EV story is mostly on two wheels. E-scooters sold a record 2.23 lakh units in October 2026, and about 11.6% of two-wheelers registered in September 2026 were electric.

pillars.title: Cars are catching up
pillars.text: Electric cars crossed 30,000 monthly sales five months in a row, reaching 36,911 in October 2026, about 7% of passenger vehicle registrations.

pillars.title: Swap and subscribe
pillars.text: Battery swapping and battery-as-a-service models such as MG Windsor's and Hero Vida's subscription options cut the upfront price.

pillars.title: Owners share what they learn
pillars.text: Owner communities trade charger reviews, trip reports and tips, which is how highway corridors like Delhi–Jaipur and Bengaluru–Mysuru became practical EV routes.

plugs.name: CCS2
plugs.use: DC fast charging. The standard for electric cars sold in India.

plugs.name: Type 2 AC
plugs.use: Slower AC charging from wall boxes and public AC posts. Good for overnight or workplace charging.

plugs.name: LECCS
plugs.use: Light electric vehicle connector for two- and three-wheelers.

plugs.name: CHAdeMO
plugs.use: Older DC standard still found on a few city hubs.

plugs.name: Bharat AC-001 / DC-001
plugs.use: Earlier low-voltage Indian standards, mostly seen on legacy three-wheelers and small cars.

roadTrip: Plan stops between roughly 20% and 80% charge. DC fast charging slows sharply above 80%.
Treat claimed range as a ceiling. Speed, hills and air conditioning cut real-world range, so keep a 10–15% buffer.
Carry a Type 2 cable and check a charger's live status in its app before you leave.
Stick to corridors with a fast charger every 25–50 km, and know your backup stop.
Keep a payment app and an RFID card from at least two charging networks.

timeline.event: FAME I launches India's first national EV incentives.
FAME II commits ₹10,000 crore to e-2W, e-3W, e-bus and charging support.
Ministry of Power issues public charging guidelines, revised in 2024.
EV manufacturing scheme for cars (March) and PM E-DRIVE (October) begin.
Electric cars pass 30,000 monthly sales; e-2W sales hit a record 2.23 lakh in October.
